title: Dynamic surge allocation guardrails and rotation policy for cycle-level capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a set of operational guardrails, decision rules, and rotation policies that allow product/engineering leads to safely trigger dynamic redistribution of staffed capacity across concurrent cycle initiatives. This ticket captures the PM-level requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for a first MVP that works across two classes of work: mission-critical SLA-backed Dedicated runway and elastic exploratory initiatives (PLG features). The goal is to enable predictable, auditable micro-tranches of staff and reserved effort that can be temporarily reallocated under well-understood conditions.
goals: Define deterministic triggers (signals + thresholds) for temporary surge allocation that preserve Dedicated SLAs
Specify rotation policy to avoid burnout and ensure knowledge continuity when staff move between initiatives
Create decision-flow documentation and an ops dashboard prototype for visibility and audit
Run tabletop simulations on 12 representative cycle scenarios and publish expected outcomes (latency, throughput, delivery slip)
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc that enumerates triggers, cooldown windows, max-surge-per-initiative and total-cycle-surge cap
Dashboard mock with per-initiative capacity allocation, recent reallocations, and rollback button
Simulation results for 12 scenarios showing: median delivery slip <= 2 business days and Dedicated latency regression <= 5%
A signed-off rollout checklist and communication plan with Eng leads and People (rotation fairness rules)
deliverables: PM spec: Dynamic Surge Allocation Guardrails (confluence) - linked
Ops dashboard prototype (Figma) with three views: current allocations, historic reallocations, what-if simulator
Decision flow runbook for on-call and product ops
Simulation report (.csv + notebook) with scenario definitions and aggregated metrics
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff with Eng & People. Agreed to prioritize Dedicated SLA protection first. Assigned simulation leads: @marco, @lin.
2026-02-28: Draft triggers proposed: utilization > 85% for 6 hours OR incident-induced capacity drop > 10% yields request for surge. People will own rotation fairness rules.
2026-03-05: Simulation scaffold ready. Early run shows naive surge allocation causes delivery slip > 5 days for non-Dedicated initiatives — added cooldown and max-surge-per-person caps.
2026-03-10: Design review with Eng leads: approved dashboard layout; asked to add immutable audit trail of reallocations for compliance teams.
2026-03-14: PM review with GTM & Customer Success. Added customer-impact classification to trigger rules; high-impact customers exempt from reallocations without Exec approval.
decisions: Rotation window set to 2-week minimum shadow + 2-week active rotation to reduce ramp churn
Max-surge cap per initiative: 15% of staffed FTEs in the initiative and global cycle cap: 8% of total org staffed capacity
Triggers will combine system signals (utilization, error rate), business signals (priority tag), and manual escalation paths
Allocations will be logged as immutable events in the console audit stream for 12 months
risks: Risk: Frequent reallocations may cause context switching and delivery slippage. Mitigation: enforce minimum rotation windows and require handover docs
Risk: Perceived unfairness across teams. Mitigation: People will run a quarterly fairness audit and publish rotation credits
Risk: Customers on Dedicated plans could be impacted. Mitigation: automatic exemption for SLA-backed customers unless Exec opt-in
Risk: Tooling complexity delays adoption. Mitigation: MVP will be conservative and manual-approval-first; automation later
notes: Trade-off: strict caps preserve SLA but reduce usefulness of surge; we aim for a pragmatic midline (8% global cap) and will revisit after 2 cycles
Operational consideration: rotation should prioritize pairs (shadow then takeover) to avoid knowledge loss
We will coordinate with Finance for visibility into cost impact of surge staffing (OT, contractor usage)
